childMarkdownRemark.html:
Vehicle dashboard is a global ford product that is a Ford owner's first start into the ownership experience. Here users can check the status of their vehicle, get help with service appointments, receive critical updates about recalls and vehicle health and gain trust with Ford on their ownership journey.

We built this product from the ground up as part of a company-wide redesign of our systems technology stack. I was put as a senior engineer of the tiger team that had an aggressive deadline to re-write the entire product in next.js using the latest and greatest web technologies.

This page involved a huge amount of integration with dozens of company systems like vehicle telemetry, recalls databases, vehicle health information, dealership data and user information. The APIs ranged from graphql, REST, SOAP, bigquery and postgres databases directly.

Stitched together the experience is seamless and we already have had millions of monthly views.

childMarkdownRemark.html:
Hapytycs is an embedded haptic motor that syncs with your GPS signal and provides realtime turn by turn directional data. Think of a bike helmet that vibrates left or right when a turn is coming. Or handlebars that can vibrate when you made a wrong turn.

The vision of haptycs is to fundamentally re-think how we interact with our environment through an new language. I worked with an LA design firm to craft the application, system and hardware required for this visionary product.

The project involved Arduino, raspberry pi and a great deal of learning how to write Swift applications that interface with the bluetooth and haptic motors.

A full stack two-sided marketplace built from scratch around big data, web scraping, ecommerce and modern UX.

In the summer of 2022 I was contacted by a recruiter to take a project from a rudimentary proof of concept to a fully functioning MVP. The client was a startup trying to capitalize on the new opportunities NCAA athletes have to get paid and establish brand partnerships.

The goal was to build something that combines the two-sided marketplace features of an app like Cameo, Turo or Upwork and the discovery tools that rely on big-data to find trending, hot or niche matches for a business to an athlete.

Businesses, agents, or athletes can come to the app, sign up and track metrics coalated to a bunch of individual scores generated by a slurry of different factors. All of the various score elements go through an algorithm to then produce a complete summary score. As the application grows the hope is to continually include more factors to create the underlying scores.

The team came to me as their founding software developer had to step down to pursue other opportunities and wanted me to take what was then several microservices and help combine them into a fully function ecosystem, all while developing the product at the same time.

Backend / Data Development

I decided to start from scratch, taking the data models assembled in a Django application as a base. The first task was to web-scrape every college athlete that existed and gather any relevant metadata pertaining to them. All of this logic was then put into lambdas to continually get new players as they came into the NCAA. We also had to develop pipelines that continually track the performance, engagement and sentiment of any relevant athlete.

Tools Used:

  • Hasura
  • Postgres Database
  • GraphQL
  • Google cloud functions
  • Python/Flask for data scraping

eCommerce Development

After the initial workflow for tracking and rating athletes, we needed two create the two-sided marketplace. This required a dashboard for both athletes and companies to create and track potential partnerships.

I started by working alongside the leadership team to generate a variety of user stories and epochs corresponding various commerce workflows. We then set up an inventory of products and variants that could potentially be purchased. I structured this data after my experience using the shopify API.

The price of each "product" is dynamic meaning that it corresponds to an algorithm based on the data of each player. Each item needed to be calculated from this formula and then cached so that it could be accessed quickly.

Tools Used:

  • Redis
  • Postgres
  • Google Sheets API
  • Figma / Material UI

An idea that combines technology, storytelling, immersive experience and art in one. I partnered with an artist/designer to help bring an idea to life.

I was honored to be a part of such an innovative and unique installation.

childMarkdownRemark.html:
This was a lesson in just how much work goes into a national broadcast spot. BlackMath contacted a few composers to write 3-5 songs for the commercial and told us that the Bai people would be choosing the best fit. About 80% through the writing the process we found out that Justin Timberlake himself would be choosing the final track!

After we locked the track, I was basically making edits around the clock. There was a point where edits where basically coming in as fast as I was making them. What I learned from this project is that keeping very organized files and versions. It was a blast and of course, now I can say I wrote a track for JT.

Doing installation work is one of my favorite things as an audio producer. Maybe it is from playing in bands my whole life. Either way, I helped collaborate with HP Innovation to create this gigantic masterpiece, debuted at New York City's "Panorama Music Festival."

We used Max for Live and Ableton all hidden away in the installation to drive the music and instrumentation. What started out with alot of frustrated hours of coding, ended with something truly magical. Watching people's faces when they interacted with the machine was very gratifying.

I hope that I can continue work like this in the future.
